result.text:
[2026-10-05] I found no concrete errors or counterexamples under the supplied specification. This is a manual review; the evaluator was unavailable.

The following behavior is valid and should remain:

- Selector lookup filters on exactly `"select"` and gives exact category matches priority over all fallback matches.
- Fallback accepts only absent, null, or empty categories. Whole-token matching handles reversed token order and prevents substring matches: `"modeling"` does not match `"model"`, while `"policy-permission"` matches `"mode"`.
- Missing-selector detection precedes blank-request handling.
- Only the request is trimmed. Choice names and values retain their whitespace.
- Flattening preserves encounter order and excludes group names and ids.
- Matching follows all four tiers in the required order and deduplicates by exact value within each tier.
- Ambiguity stops resolution. For example, choices with values `"FAST"` and `"Fast"` make request `"fast"` ambiguous at the case-insensitive value tier, even if a choice name exactly matches only at a weaker tier.
- Exact matches override weaker matches. Values `"A"` and `"a"` resolve request `"A"` to `"A"`.
- Empty-string choice values are handled correctly when matched through a nonblank name.
- The resolved value is compared exactly with `currentValue`; an unlisted current value never becomes an implicit choice.

The implementation is synchronous, self-contained, and uses no prohibited facilities. No corrective change is justified by this review.
